newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium follows LME down despite weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium follows LME down despite weak yen.

text.p: Tokyo aluminium futures closed lower on Monday after lacklustre trade, with a decline on the London Metal Exchange on Friday more than offsetting the dollar's continued strength against the yen, traders said.
Prices fell 2.3 yen to 1.1 yen, with the benchmark February 1998 contract down 1.1 yen at 207.0 yen per kg.
The decline came despite a renewed depreciation of the yen, which was trading well above 126 yen against the dollar by the close of TOCOM, compared with below 126 yen earlier in the day.
Trading volume fell further with only 2,517 lots changing hands by 0645 GMT, down sharply from 4,602 on Friday and 19,645 a week ago when the contracts were traded for the first time.
"It was quiet. People are waiting to see what will happen in London today," said one trader. "But I don't think there's much downside. There's support between 200 and 203 yen."
The trader added the new contract should attract more trade once aluminium prices start recovering.
